h1: Before and After Video Maker: Show the Change Your Product Makes
lead: This before and after video maker shows the problem, then the fix. A cluttered drawer gets organized, a bare wall gets a shelf, a worn car seat gets a cover, all in one short clip.
intro: A before-and-after video shows two moments in a row: how things look without your product, then how they look with it. It's a simple story that shoppers follow in seconds. A tangled cable mess becomes a tidy desk. A greasy grill grate gets scrubbed clean. An empty balcony lights up with your string lights.

Start with a photo of the product, then write both halves as one line, such as “messy closet shelf, then folded sweaters in our fabric bins.” Choose 6, 10, 15, or 30 seconds and 9:16, 1:1, 16:9, 4:3, or 3:4 so each state has room to register.

faq.q: What products work for before and after videos?
faq.a: Products that make a visible change to a space or object: closet and pantry organizers, cleaning brushes, furniture covers, wall shelves, lighting, and car accessories.

faq.q: How do I describe the before and the after?
faq.a: Use one sentence with two parts joined by “then.” For example: “cluttered entryway with shoes everywhere, then shoes lined up on our bamboo rack.”

faq.q: Can I make before and after videos for skincare or weight loss products?
faq.a: We'd advise against it. Many ad platforms restrict before-and-after content about skin, body, or health results, and the change shown should always be one your product really makes. Show how the product is used rather than promising an outcome.
Yes, add them after you download, in CapCut or TikTok. Typed labels stay crisp and correctly spelled, which AI-generated lettering can't always manage.

overview.h2: Make the product’s job visible in two beats
overview.p: Before-and-after works for products that change a space, object, or arrangement in a way a viewer can recognize quickly. Name the starting condition first, then show the finished condition with the product present and the same subject still easy to compare.

overview.h2: Keep the promise inside the frame
overview.p: Use this format for organizing, cleaning, installing, covering, lighting, or styling. Avoid claims about a person’s body, skin, health, or guaranteed performance; show the physical change your product is actually designed to make.
